harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 with a hardened, chrooted Python web application running as locked, non-login account appsvc on TCP 8080. It starts automatically at boot and recovered successfully after a verified node reboot. RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, SELinux enforcing, SSH access, and protected configuration were preserved.
actions_performed: Created locked system account appsvc with /sbin/nologin and no home directory.
Built a root-owned chroot using the already-installed Python 3.12 runtime; no OS or kernel upgrade was performed.
Installed root-owned application content and a hardened systemd service using RootDirectory=/srv/app-chroot.
Authorized TCP 8080 through SELinux and the active/permanent firewalld public zone.
Verified HTTP 200 behavior, appsvc UID/GID, zero capabilities, chroot confinement, and denied content writes and account login.
Rebooted node1 safely, observed a changed boot ID, and verified automatic service and data recovery.
Removed temporary test artifacts and repeated final HTTP, listener, SSH, and failed-unit checks.

evidence.requirement: Web application runs inside the chroot as unprivileged appsvc on port 8080
evidence.summary: HTTP requests return 200 with the expected marker; the live process is UID/GID 992, has zero capabilities, and its root inode matches /srv/app-chroot. Only its Python process listens on port 8080.

evidence.requirement: Starts at boot without an interactive login session
evidence.summary: The unit is enabled and active after reboot with zero restarts and successful exit status. appsvc uses /sbin/nologin, has a locked password, no login audit session, and direct login is denied.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained unchanged. The application uses the existing RHEL Python 3.12.9 runtime; the OS-release checksum was preserved.

evidence.requirement: Security controls, administrative access, and cleanup
evidence.summary: SELinux remains enforcing with no post-boot AVCs; 8080 is labeled http_port_t and allowed persistently by firewalld. SSH remains active with its configuration checksum unchanged, zero units are failed, and no test residue remains.

Pre-restart boot ID and healthy service/data baseline were captured; the native safe reboot was acknowledged; the boot ID changed from 6ab6a71b-188c-48ae-971b-a6bb378b1d72 to 8e03a6dc-bac3-44e3-a72d-6ad0299b7b2a; service, content, HTTP response, listener, chroot identity, SSH, and system health recovered.
